items.title: CONSENT CALENDAR

Accept work performed by Cratus Inc., under Contract No. WD-2718, 8-Inch Ductile Iron Pipe and 24-Inch Earthquake Resistant Ductile Iron Pipe Water Main Installation on Prospect, Fair and Coso Avenues and Coleridge Street, for a total contract amount of $8,337,953 and a final contract duration of 690 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and 11 months); and authorize final payment to the contractor. (Robinson)

Approve an increase in the amount of $450,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 60 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WD-2843, 16-, 12-, and 8-Inch Ductile Iron Water Main Replacement on Diamond St from 27th Street to Diamond Heights Blvd, 28th and Duncan Streets from Douglass to Noe Streets, Valley Street from Diamond to Noe Streets, and Noe Street from Duncan to Valley Streets, with M Squared Construction Inc., for a new total contract amount limit of up to $10,132,240 and a new contract duration limit of up to 789 consecutive calendar days (approximately two years and two months), to address remaining work scope associated with San Francisco Public Works paving restoration within the project work limits and potential future change orders associated with differing site conditions. (Robinson)

Approve Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. PRO.0070, NERC Compliance and Audit Support, with Archer Energy Solutions, LLC, increasing the contract amount by $1,500,000 and extending the contract duration by one year, for a total not-to-exceed contract amount of $9,500,000 and a total contract duration of six years, for increased contract usage and a higher than expected spending rate as a result of hiring additional part-time consultants due to loss of San Francisco Public Utilities Commission staff. (Ritchie)

Approve an increase of $7,000,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 596 calendar days (approximately one year and eight months) to the duration contingency for Contract No. WW-639, Oceanside Water Pollution Control Plant Digester Gas Utilization Upgrades, with Monterey Mechanical Co., for a new contract duration limit of up to 2,593 consecutive calendar days (approximately seven years and one month) and a contract amount limit of up to $54,293,900. The proposed contingency increase will address additional costs for a cogeneration system, associated mechanical and electrical system modifications and related PG&E electrical interconnection equipment compliance, and to allow additional time for the contractor to procure long-lead mechanical and electrical equipment to comply with PG&E electrical interconnection requirements. (Robinson)

Approve an increase in the amount of $2,500,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 100 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WW-736, Castro and Mission Districts Sewer Improvements, with Precision Engineering, Inc., increasing the contract amount limit up to $10,499,552 and increasing the contract duration limit up to 567 consecutive calendar days (approximately one year and seven months), to rehabilitate an additional 1,440 linear feet of large diameter high-risk sewers on 18th Street between Eureka and Danvers Streets. Implementation of all the 18th Street sewer rehabilitation under a single construction contract will reduce disruption to the Castro District residents and businesses. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the 18th Street sewer rehabilitation work for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. (Robinson)

Approve a seven-year revocable license to Pacesetter, Inc. to use approximately 37,000 square feet of SFPUC Parcel No. 172 located adjacent to the property at 645 Almanor Avenue in Sunnyvale, California to maintain a parking lot and landscaping for an annual use fee of $93,240, subject to four-percent annual increases. (Flynn)

Award Contract No. CS-1414, Project Labor Agreement Upcountry Training Services with San Joaquin County Office of Education, in the amount not to exceed $1,000,000 with a duration of five years, to provide pre-apprentice training, barrier removal, and referral services for Tuolumne County and the surrounding areas of San Francisco Public Utilities Commission service territory. (Robinson)

Award Contract No. HH-1013, Moccasin Compound Water System Filtration Addition, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, Sierra Mountain Construction, Inc., in the amount of $4,177,936, and with a duration of 346 consecutive calendar days to install a permanent freshwater treatment plant in Moccasin, CA. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. (Ritchie) Commissioner Stacy stated she requested clarification on Items 7c and 7g and Margaret Hannaford had provided her with the needed information. President Paulson commented on Item 7g with regards to the apprenticeship program and Upcountry
Award Contract No. WD-2897, Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant Ozonation, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, J.F. Shea Construction, Inc amount of $234,782,000
items.text: Award Contract No. WD-2897, Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant Ozonation, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, J.F. Shea Construction, Inc., in the amount of $234,782,000, and with a duration of 1,612 consecutive calendar days (approximately four years and five months), to construct an ozone treatment facility to control taste and odor in the raw water supplied to the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant. (Ritchie) Bryan Dessaure, Project Manager, stated the primary objective of this project is to install a ozone treatment facility as a long-term solution to control taste and odor in the water supplied. President Paulson thanked Project Manager Dessaure for the explanations and further analysis provided in the report. Commissioner Ajami congratulated Project Manager Dessaure on this being the first design bid build project. She also questioned the bid process and incentives we offer bidders, while still attempting to minimize risk factors; Stephen Robinson, Assistant General Manager for Infrastructure, provided clarity on these concerns. Nicole Sandkulla, CEO of Bay Area Water Supply and Conservation Agency (BAWSCA), provided remote public comment in support of this project and stated she was looking forward to its completion. On the motion to approve the Item #8:

items.title: Approve Amendment No. 4 to Contract No. CS-247(R), Customer and Administrative Services for Community Choice Aggregation Program, with Calpine Energy Solutions, LLC
items.text: Approve Amendment No. 4 to Contract No. CS-247(R), Customer and Administrative Services for Community Choice Aggregation Program, with Calpine Energy Solutions, LLC, for continued meter data management, billing, and customer care support for the CleanPowerSF program, increasing the contract amount by $2,500,000 and extending the contract’s duration by six months, for a total not-to-exceed amount of $35,145,425 and total duration of nine years and six months, subject to approval by the Board of Supervisors under Charter Section 9.118. (Hale) Andrew Bevington, CleanPowerSF Customer Solutions Manager, stated this amendment would allow his team to issue an RFP to secure a new contract and the continuity of operations should CleanPowerSF need to transition Calpine’s functions to a new company. Commissioner Ajami questioned how we could bring more generalized solutions to the table and further questioned the location of the meters and the metering itself. On the motion to approve the Item #9:

items.title: Consider and adopt the proposed Wholesale Water Rates for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, which will become effective for meter readings on or after July 1, 2024
items.text: Consider and adopt the proposed Wholesale Water Rates for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, which will become effective for meter readings on or after July 1, 2024. The San Francisco Public Utilities Commission developed the proposed rates in accordance with the terms of the Water Supply Agreement between the City and County of San Francisco and its Wholesale Customers, which the Commission approved on April 28, 2009, by Resolution No. 09-0069, and amended and restated on January 26, 2021, by Resolution No. 21-0009, with subsequent approval by the Wholesale Customers. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that this action is exempt from the CEQA. If the item is approved, the Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision. (Hom)
